title: What are Objects?
overview: Objects are data structures used to store related information in key-value pairs. They are commonly used to represent real-world entities in JavaScript applications.

title: Creating and Accessing Objects
overview: Objects can be created using curly braces. Values inside objects are accessed using dot notation or bracket notation.

title: Adding and Updating Object Properties
overview: Object properties can be added or updated after an object is created by assigning new values to keys.

example.title: Update Object

title: Object Methods
overview: Functions stored inside objects are called methods. They allow objects to perform actions using their stored data.

example.title: Object Method Example

title: Object Destructuring
overview: Object destructuring allows developers to extract properties from objects and store them directly in variables using a shorter syntax.

example.title: Destructuring Example

title: Object Utility Methods
overview: JavaScript provides built-in methods to work with objects, such as getting keys, values, and entries.

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned how objects store data, access and modify properties, create methods, use destructuring, and work with built-in object methods.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ Objects store data as key-value pairs.
✔ Properties can be added or updated.
✔ Objects can contain methods.
✔ Destructuring extracts values easily.
✔ Object methods help manage data.
